wins: Mapped internal network topology with initial nmap sweep, identifying three hosts in the 172.16.5.0/24 range and their open ports (ep001_step03, ep001_step05)
Captured initial service banners on host 172.16.5.12, confirming SSH and HTTP versions for future targeting (ep001_step07)
fails: Unable to escalate privileges on target 172.16.5.12 due to lack of valid SSH credentials and no recognized exploit chain (ep001_step12, ep001_step15)
Repeated mentor intervention to resume reconnaissance after losing session persistence, indicating deficient session management strategy (ep001_step09, ep001_step13)
Failed to exploit web application due to ineffective payload delivery and missing input sanitization insights (ep001_step11)
key_outcomes.summary: Reconnaissance phase partially successful with detailed service enumeration, but inability to obtain valid credentials or exploit services stalled progression, warranting focused credential harvesting and exploitation experimentation.

repeated_failure_patterns.pattern: Multiple attempts to maintain session persistence on 172.16.5.12 failed because SSH credentials were not harvested or reused effectively.

skill_cards.if_condition: When an SSH banner is exposed on a reachable host
skill_cards.then_action: Perform targeted SSH enumeration with nmap scripting to validate authentication methods and banner versions

skill_cards.if_condition: When HTTP service responds with status 200 and directory listing disabled
skill_cards.then_action: Run gobuster with wordlist apt base + extensions, then capture HTTP response bodies for injection markers

skill_cards.if_condition: When multiple open ports identified during initial scan
skill_cards.then_action: Prioritize further scans with nmap args '-A -p-' to uncover additional services and guess OS reliably

memory_ops.reason: High success capturing SSH metadata during reconnaissance, valuable for follow-up credential strategies.

next_experiments.title: Credential Harvesting via SSH Banner Analysis
next_experiments.description: Use collected SSH banner details to try default/public keys against the host (ssh -i /path/to/cataloged_key user@172.16.5.12) and combine with Hydra multi-user brute-force leveraging captured user list to obtain valid credentials.

next_experiments.title: Web Service Injection Testing
next_experiments.description: Automate POST injection payloads against identified HTTP endpoints using Burp Suite Intruder with payloads from the top 50 common web shells to find unsanitized input.

next_experiments.title: Session Recovery After SSH Disruption
next_experiments.description: Deploy netcat reverse shell listener post-exploitation and script keep-alive checks (while loop + cron) so future SSH sessions survive brief disruptions.
